title: Job 31
paragraphs: ¹ "I made a covenant with my eyes — how then could I look with desire on a young woman? ² For what is God's portion from above, his inheritance from the Almighty on high? ³ Is it not ruin for the wicked and disaster for those who do evil? ⁴ Does he not see my ways and count every step I take? ⁵ If I have walked in falsehood or if my feet have rushed toward deceit —

⁶ then let God weigh me in honest scales and he will know my integrity. ⁷ If my steps have turned from the path, if my heart has followed my eyes, if any stain has clung to my hands, ⁸ then let me sow and another eat, and let my crops be uprooted. ⁹ If my heart has been seduced by a woman and I have lurked at my neighbor's door, ¹⁰ then let my wife be another man's slave, and let others sleep with her.

¹¹ For that would have been a wicked crime, an offense worthy of judgment. ¹² It is a fire that burns down to destruction and would consume everything I have planted. ¹³ If I have dismissed the claims of my servants when they brought a grievance against me, ¹⁴ what then will I do when God confronts me? What will I answer when he calls me to account? ¹⁵ Did not the one who made me make them too? Did not the same God form us both in the womb?

¹⁶ If I have denied what the poor desired, or let the widow's eyes grow dim with weeping, ¹⁷ if I have eaten my food alone without sharing it with the fatherless — ¹⁸ but from my youth I raised the orphan like a father, and from birth I guided the widow — ¹⁹ if I have watched someone die for lack of clothing, or left the poor without a coat to wear, ²⁰ and his back has not blessed me for the warmth of my wool —

²¹ if I have raised my hand against the fatherless, knowing that men stood by me in the gate, ²² then let my arm fall from my shoulder and be broken at the joint. ²³ For I dreaded calamity from God; I could not endure his majesty. ²⁴ If I have put my confidence in gold or said to pure gold, "You are my security" — ²⁵ if I rejoiced because my wealth was great or because my own hand had won so much —

²⁶ if I looked at the sun in its radiance or the moon moving in splendor, ²⁷ and my heart was secretly enticed and my hand kissed my lips in worship — ²⁸ that too would have been an iniquity worthy of judgment, for I would have been unfaithful to God above. ²⁹ Have I rejoiced at my enemy's misfortune or gloated when disaster struck him? ³⁰ No — I never let my mouth sin by calling down a curse on him.

³¹ If the men of my household have never said, 'Who has not been filled by Job's generosity?' — ³² no stranger ever had to sleep in the street, for I opened my door to every traveler. ³³ If I have concealed my sin the way Adam did, hiding my guilt in my heart — ³⁴ if I have been so afraid of the crowd or so terrified of what people might think that I kept silent and stayed indoors — ³⁵ Oh, if only someone would listen to me! Here is my plea — let the Almighty answer me. Let my accuser put his charges in writing.

³⁶ I would carry that document on my shoulder; I would wear it like a crown. ³⁷ I would give him a full account of all my steps; I would approach him like a prince. ³⁸ If my land cries out against me and its furrows weep together, ³⁹ if I have eaten its harvest without payment or crushed the life out of those who worked it — ⁴⁰ then let thorns grow where wheat once grew and weeds where barley should stand. The words of Job are ended.
